solution.brief:
MESH CONSTRAINTS
Mesh constraints allow to constrain the growth of an aggregation
only inside or outside (set by the IN input) of a given closed mesh.
Constraints can be "soft", meaning that only the centroid of the part
is checked against the constraint, or "hard", meaning that also the geometry
is checked for intersections (set by the SOFT input).
Additionally, the REQ input can be used to define if a constraint is necessary
or optional. If using a mis of necessary and optional constraints, the aggregation
will try to place all parts which have all necessary constraints satisfyed, and
at least one of the optional ones.
